name: amparo-demo

scripts.build:chain: npm run copy-zk && npm run build

comment:overrides: Same block as the contract package, and load-bearing for the same reason: each wasm
package carries its own instance owning its own classes, so an object built by one copy
fails the other's internal type check - 'expected instance of LedgerParameters' - from
inside a dependency, mid-transaction, with nothing pointing at the duplication.
It is repeated here rather than inherited because the two packages keep separate
node_modules trees on purpose. An npm workspace would hoist them into one, which is the
arrangement that reintroduces the duplicate in the first place.
Verify with: npm run check-wasm. Not `npm ls`, which reads one tree and cannot see the
case that matters: the bundle draws from BOTH trees, so two trees each holding a single
version can still hold two DIFFERENT versions while every per-tree check reports success.
Neither the typecheck nor the tests can see any of it - they never build a transaction.
